acceptance_criteria_proven: stable idempotency key per scheduled occurrence: routine:{job_id}:{scheduled_instant} default, custom template must contain {scheduled_instant} (a template without it would collapse all occurrences into one task — refused fail-closed)

catch-up {skip,once,all-bounded}: skip materializes nothing for a missed gap (logged no-op with reason), once creates one catch-up card (default), all-bounded walks the schedule backwards (interval and cron expressions, configured zone, DST fall-back fold guard preferring the later instant still before the fire) bounded by catch_up_bound 1..20 default 5, stopping at the first slot that already has a card — an outage can never flood the board

no duplicate on an open identical run: a task with the occurrence key that already exists (open or done) is read back through tasks.idempotency_key (same predicate create_task applies), never duplicated — the healing path for a lost answer/crash between commit and response; the routine_occurrence provenance event is written only on creation so the audit trail stays exactly-once too

no-agent routines stay deterministic scripts: the script IS the job (unchanged no_agent semantics, stdout delivered as usual) and kanban work appears ONLY on exception — a failed run creates ONE exception card with the script output (deduped on the same occurrence key); a failure on a skipped catch-up occurrence creates no card

existing cron scheduler reused: the bridge is one hook in _prepare_job_prompt running BEFORE the config gate (a corrupt config.yaml cannot stop deterministic board maintenance) and before the no_agent short-circuit; no second scheduler engine, no dispatcher changes, occurrence identity rides the existing _scheduled_instant claim plumbing and the executions-ledger at-most-once guarantee

CLI/API/tool read+create paths: hermes cron create/edit --kanban-* (merge-over-stored-block semantics, --kanban-clear), 'Kanban routine' row in cron list detail, cronjob_manage kanban property (dict replaces / {} clears on update, shown in cronjob list), create_job/update_job as the single validation chokepoint every path shares, cross-field shape re-validated on any payload edit of a merged record

old cron jobs unchanged: jobs without a kanban block are byte-identical (block stored only when configured; TestLegacyJobsUnchanged proves stored records and create/edit without the block never carry it) and the full tests/cron/ tree passes unchanged
